finding_key: packages/backend/src/api/v1/documents.controller.ts::mass assignment into prisma `updatedocument` on the v1 patch route (pre-existing, but it is the other call site of the method this diff changed)
evidence: In packages/backend/src/api/v1/documents.controller.ts the PATCH handler declares `@Body() body: { title?: string }` and passes it verbatim as `data: body` to `DocumentService.updateDocument`. Because an inline type literal emits `design:paramtypes = Object`, Nest's ValidationPipe (configured with whitelist/forbidNonWhitelisted in packages/backend/src/main.ts) skips validation for that metatype, so arbitrary `Prisma.DocumentUpdateInput` keys — notably `workspace: { connect: { id } }` and `author: { connect: { id } }` — reach Prisma unchecked; `getDocumentOrThrow({ id, workspaceId })` only validates the document's current workspace, not the reconnect target. The sibling legacy route in document/document.controller.ts does allowlist fields and re-runs `assertMember` on `body.workspaceId`, confirming the asymmetry the claim describes. One caveat: WorkspaceScopeGuard was not supplied, so the last step of the exploit narrative (guard checks only the route param) is inferred rather than read; the mass-assignment sink itself is directly verified. Note the attacker-supplied `updatedAt` specifically is neutralized by the diff's `{ ...data, updatedAt: new Date() }` spread.
